section_1.title: Introduction: The 'Why' of Clarity
section_1.content: A brief hook explaining that math is a language. Effective explanation isn't just about truth; it's about transmission. We define the goal: minimizing cognitive load while maximizing conceptual retention.
section_1.example: Comparing a messy, text-heavy manual vs. an intuitive IKEA-style graphic assembly guide for a robot.

section_2.title: Criterion 1: The Principle of Gradual Abstraction
section_2.content: Introduce prerequisite knowledge mapping. Never jump to symbols before building a concrete mental model. Use visual animations to show transitions from 'Physical Object' to 'Geometric Model' to 'Algebraic Formula'.
section_2.example: Explaining the concept of Area: Start with counting square blocks on a grid, then move to a rectangle shape, finally arriving at the formula A = l × w.

section_3.title: Criterion 2: Visual-Spatial Encoding
section_3.content: Discuss the 'Dual Coding Theory'. Explanations must pair verbal descriptions with spatial representations. Use animation to highlight how a graph 'breathes' when a variable in a function changes.
section_3.example: Visualizing the Sine function: An animation of a 'Math-Cat' running around a circle, with the y-coordinate being plotted simultaneously on a Cartesian graph to the right.

section_4.title: Criterion 3: The 'So-What' Connection
section_4.content: Ensure every mathematical concept is grounded in a logical sequence. Use a 'Constraint Check': Does the audience understand the limitations and valid ranges of the concept?
section_4.example: When teaching division by zero, use an animation of a hungry 'Robo-Chef' trying to distribute 10 cookies into 0 jars. Show the system error visual to emphasize the logical boundary.

section_5.title: Summary & Application: The 3-Step Checklist
section_5.content: Conclude with a summary checklist for any explanation: 1. Concrete Base (Prerequisites), 2. Visual Linkage, 3. Logical Boundaries. Encouraging the creation of a 'Mental Map' for students.
section_5.example: The 'Checklist Mascot': An owl icon that appears on screen summarizing: [Anchor to Reality] -> [Visual Translation] -> [Boundary Check].

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text("- " + line, font_size=24, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The 'Why' of Clarity", ["Math is a universal language.", "Effective teaching requires clarity.", "We focus on minimizing cognitive load."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show title 'Introduction: The Why of Clarity' (#FFFFFF) - Already done by setup_layout
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF") # Light Blue
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Fade in a simple thought bubble icon (#FFD700).
        bubble = SVGMobject(path="thought_bubble.svg") if False else Circle(radius=0.5, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(bubble, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(bubble))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700") # Gold
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display text: 'Clarity drives understanding' (#FFFFFF).
        clarity_text = Text("Clarity drives understanding", font_size=28, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(clarity_text, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(clarity_text))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00") # Lime Green
        self.wait(1)

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
